text:
incident-bot: SEV2 paging: network-high — 1 customer impacted (HelioCorp, private VPC) — 504s from app endpoint via private NLB. Please acknowledge if oncall.

sara_ops: acked. seeing spike in 504s starting ~10:12 UTC, affects the /api/v1/ingest path only. HelioCorp uses private deploy in us-west-2 with NLB fronting our private ALB+ecs.

liu_support: customer-ops reached out — they see bursts of connections dropping, backend healthchecks flipping healthy->unhealthy. reported after firewall rule change on their side ~09:50.

priya_neteng: looking at VPC flow logs — lots of SYNs to targets, then RSTs from targets back to source. looks like asymmetric routing: responses going out different interface and getting dropped by customer's firewall.

josh_platform: that matches an NLB target healthcheck failure pattern. NLB preserves source IP, so if responses route via a different NAT or peering, firewall will block.

alex_se: customer-ops says they changed egress SMT policy to force egress via an on-prem gateway. might be the cause.

sara_ops: quick customer impact summary for handoff: ~15% of requests to HelioCorp ingest path failing intermittently, no data loss yet, retries succeed for some. customer reporting degraded UX for ingestion.

priya_neteng: triage plan: 1) avoid making customer firewall changes. 2) attempt to reduce asymmetry by forcing response path back through same ENI for targets via source/destination checks or SNATing. 3) temporary mitigation: switch traffic to a dedicated private pool (same region) that does SNAT so responses return via expected path. 4) if needed flip DNS weight to dedicated pool.

josh_platform: quick check — target group healthcheck: currently TCP 443, interval 10s, unhealthy 2. If customer firewall blocks response path, healthcheck fails quickly. we can change to HTTP GET /health?token=redwood-helio with Host header to get app-level check that responds and keeps target healthy while we fix routing.

commands from priya_neteng: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:1111:targetgroup/tg-helio/abcd1234 --health-check-protocol HTTP --health-check-path "/health?token=redwood-helio" --health-check-interval-seconds 6 --health-check-unhealthy-threshold-count 2```

priya_neteng: also adding SG rule to allow ephemeral ports from NLB ENI range to target to avoid RSTs while routing is sorted: ```aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc123 --protocol tcp --port 32768-61000 --cidr 100.96.0.0/11``` (CIDR = our internal ENI range)

liu_support: alerting HelioCorp: we will attempt a non-disruptive healthcheck switch and open ephemeral ports. will request they standby for a possible DNS weight flip in 20m if issues persist.

customer-ops: noted, will keep their netops on call. they can temporarily allow traffic from our SNAT egress if we need.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by josh_platform: healthcheck-update (dry-run) -> staged. CI: green.

sara_ops: performing change now. expect brief flapping while NLB marks targets healthy/unhealthy.

(5m passes)

priya_neteng: healthcheck changed and SG updated. early sign: target group now shows healthy for 4/4 targets. KPM: error rate for /api/v1/ingest dropped from 15%->6%.

liu_support: customer confirms partial improvement but still seeing occasional 504s every ~2-3 minutes.

josh_platform: likely some responses still egressing via on-prem gateway. Next mitigation: route-based failover — move HelioCorp VIP to private dedicated pool that SNATs outbound so asymmetry resolved. This is higher-impact; will coordinate TTL and DNS weight.

alex_se: if we do dedicated pool, we can maintain session stickiness for a time and avoid cutting state. estimate <5m for failover once DNS weight flipped to 100%.

sara_ops: stakeholder check — do we have go from customer for DNS flip?

customer-ops: HelioCorp authorizes failover to dedicated pool now. they accept risk.

priya_neteng: executing route change: updating routing table and internal service weights. commands: ```curl -XPOST https://internal-routing.prod.redwood/api/v1/weights -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ROUTER_TOKEN}" -d '{"vip":"helio-ingest.prod","weights":{"private-dedicated":100,"private-nlb":0}}'```

deploy-bot: routing change applied, propagation started. TTL = 30s.

(30s)

liu_support: monitoring — error rate down to 0.8%, latency normalizing. HelioCorp confirms ingestion is back to normal.

josh_platform: rollback plan if dedicated pool shows issues: revert weights to original and re-open ephemeral SG. also prepare to restore SNAT off if cost/traffic concerns.

sara_ops: post-mortem notes to gather: timeline of firewall change on customer side, VPC flow logs showing asymmetric routes, healthcheck behaviour, why initial healthchecks didn't surface asymmetry earlier, cost delta for SNAT in dedicated pool, recommended guardrails (require egress route verification before changes).

priya_neteng: follow-ups: 1) add an internal doc about asymmetric routing patterns and mitigation steps. 2) add a canary healthcheck that validates path symmetry (source IP echo). 3) update runbook for private NLB to include immediate SNAT-based failover option.

alex_se: I will draft customer-facing summary and recommend they avoid forcing egress changes without coordination.

sara_ops: handing off to josh for on-call night cover. josh — summary: HelioCorp ingest 504s caused by asymmetric egress after customer firewall change. Mitigations applied: healthcheck -> HTTP, ephemeral SG open, failover to dedicated SNAT pool. Service stable, monitor for 3 hours.

josh_platform: ack. I'll own until 03:30 UTC. escalation path: priya_neteng and sara_ops. tagging for PM/infra follow-ups.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SEV2 -> monitoring. assigned: josh_platform. next update in 30m or on status change. :white_check_mark:
